title: Turning away from the signs is a choice with an end.
subtitle: The other side of the promise to Adam's children
then: Right after the promise to whoever follows guidance comes its opposite. Ibn Kathir pairs it with the verse that {trap}whoever turns from My reminder will have a hard life{/trap}. Those who deny the signs remain in the Fire with no way out.
now: You know the reminder is true. You hear it in a khutbah, read it in a verse your friend shares. {trap}Then you scroll past.{/trap} The verse is sober about where a lifetime of scrolling past leads. {reward}The door to follow is still open today.{/reward}
old: Ignoring reminders is harmless as long as I do not reject them outright.
new: Turning away again and again is a path, and it has a destination.
try: The next reminder that reaches you today, stop and act on one word of it.

title: Remember the favor, keep your side, fear only Him.
subtitle: A call to the children of a righteous father
then: Israel is Prophet Ya'qub. Ibn Kathir says the call is like saying: {idea}O children of a righteous servant, be like your father and follow the truth.{/idea} Abu Al-'Aliyah said the favor was sending them prophets and books.
now: Your grandfather was the imam of the village. Your mother never missed a prayer. {trap}It is easy to feel their goodness counts for you.{/trap} {idea}This verse says: honor them by becoming like them.{/idea}
old: I come from a religious family, so I am basically fine.
new: A righteous family is a reminder to live up to, not a cover for me.
try: Pick one good habit of a parent or grandparent and do it today in their honor.

title: Do not sell guidance for a small price.
subtitle: Believing what confirms what you already have

row.title: do not be first to deny
a small price
sub: anything is small next to it

then: Those who had earlier scripture were told to believe in the Quran, {idea}which confirms what was already with them.{/idea} They were warned {trap}not to be the first to reject it, nor to trade Allah's signs for a small gain.{/trap}
now: You stay quiet about the truth in a meeting to keep your bonus. You skip a prayer to finish a sale. {trap}It always feels like a good deal at the time.{/trap} {idea}Whatever the price, it is small compared to what you sold.{/idea}
old: Bending a little on my principles for a big gain is just being practical.
new: Anything I get by selling out on Allah's guidance is a small price.
try: Notice one moment today when you are tempted to trade a principle for comfort. Keep the principle.

title: Half truth mixed with a lie is still a lie.
subtitle: Mixing truth with falsehood, and hiding what you know
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah forbade two things here and {idea}ordered them to make the truth known and explain it.{/idea} Ibn 'Abbas said: {trap}do not mix the truth with falsehood, and the facts with lies.{/trap}
now: Your CV says you led the project. You were on the team. The review you write online is true, minus the part that matters. {trap}A fact with a lie folded in.{/trap} {idea}Or silence when you know someone is being misled.{/idea}
old: As long as nothing I said was an outright lie, I was honest.
new: Mixing truth with spin, or hiding what I know, is not honesty.
try: Correct one exaggeration you have made, in a bio, a story, or a message.

title: Pray, give, and bow together with others.
subtitle: Worship joined to a community
then: Muqatil said the command meant {idea}to pray behind the Prophet ﷺ, give zakah, and bow down with his community.{/idea} Ibn Kathir explains it as a call to be with, and among, the believers.
now: You pray at home, alone, between emails. That is good. {idea}But there is something in standing shoulder to shoulder in a row of strangers.{/idea} The verse does not only say bow. It says bow with those who bow.
old: My worship is between me and Allah; other people do not matter.
new: Worship is personal, and it is also shared with the people who bow beside me.
try: Pray one prayer today with others, at a masjid, at work, or with your family.

title: You tell others to do good and forget yourself.
subtitle: Preaching without practicing
then: Ibn Jurayj said this was about people who {trap}told others to pray and fast but did not do it themselves.{/trap} His advice: {idea}whoever commands righteousness, let him be among the first to do it.{/idea}
now: You forward the hadith about patience, then shout at the driver who cut you off. You lecture your kids about screen time from behind your phone. {trap}The words go out, but do not come home.{/trap}
old: Reminding others is good, even if I am not doing it myself.
new: The first person my reminders should reach is me.
try: Think of the last piece of advice you gave someone. Do it yourself today.

title: When it is heavy, lean on patience and prayer.
subtitle: Two kinds of help, and why prayer feels hard
then: 'Umar bin Al-Khattab said there are two kinds of patience: {reward}good patience when disaster strikes, and better patience in avoiding what Allah forbade.{/reward} Prayer is among the best means of help. {trap}It is heavy, except for the humble.{/trap}
now: Bad news on the phone. A craving you have fought for weeks. Your first move is to scroll, eat, vent. {idea}This verse offers two other tools: hold on, and go pray.{/idea} If prayer feels heavy, that is exactly what the verse said.
old: Prayer is the last thing I feel like doing when I am stressed.
new: Prayer and patience are the help, especially when I do not feel like it.
try: When the next stressful moment hits today, pray two rak'ahs before doing anything else.

title: Prayer gets lighter when you know who you are meeting.
subtitle: What makes the humble different
then: The previous verse said prayer is heavy except for the humble. {idea}This verse explains them: they are certain they will meet their Lord and return to Him.{/idea} That certainty is what makes the weight bearable.
now: You drag yourself to Fajr like a chore. Now picture going to meet someone you love, who is waiting for you. {idea}The alarm is the same. What changes is knowing who you are going to.{/idea}
old: I need more discipline to pray properly.
new: Remembering that I will meet Allah makes prayer lighter.
try: Before your next prayer, take ten seconds to remember: I am about to stand before my Lord.

title: Being chosen is a reminder, not a privilege to coast on.
subtitle: Favor given to earlier generations
then: Allah reminds the Children of Israel of the favor given to their forefathers. Abu Al-'Aliyah said it was {reward}kingship, messengers and books given to them over the kingdoms of their time{/reward}, for every period has its nation.
now: You were born into faith, or found it. You have a Quran on your phone in your own language. {reward}That is a favor many never had.{/reward} {idea}The verse asks you to remember it, not to feel superior because of it.{/idea}
old: Being Muslim makes me better than others.
new: Being given guidance is a favor that asks for gratitude and effort, not pride.
try: Thank Allah today for one specific way He guided you that you did not earn.

title: On that Day, no one can carry you.
subtitle: No substitute, no ransom, no rescue
then: After the favors, a warning. Ibn Kathir cites the verse that {trap}no father can avail his son, nor a son his father{/trap}, and calls it a great warning. No one bears another's burden.
now: You assume your mother's duas will cover you. Your father's charity. Your spouse's piety. {trap}They are blessings, but they are theirs.{/trap} {idea}On that Day, you stand with what you did.{/idea} {reward}So start building it today.{/reward}
old: My family's goodness will help me on the Day.
new: On that Day I stand with my own deeds, so I must build them now.
try: Do one good deed today that is only yours: a private charity, a quiet prayer.

title: Saved from the worst, and the saving was a test too.
subtitle: Rescue from Pharaoh's cruelty
then: Ibn Kathir says Pharaoh, fearing a man from the Children of Israel would end his rule, {trap}ordered every newborn boy killed and forced them into humiliating labor.{/trap} {reward}Allah saved them through Musa.{/reward} The verse calls it all a great trial.
now: You came through the illness, the redundancy, the hard years. {reward}You are on the other side now.{/reward} {idea}The test is not only how you held up in the hard part. It is also what you do with the rescue.{/idea}
old: Once the hard time is over, the test is over.
new: Being saved from hardship is also a test of how grateful I will be.
try: Remember one hardship Allah brought you through. Do one thing today out of gratitude for it.

title: The sea split, and they watched the danger disappear.
subtitle: A rescue seen with their own eyes
then: This is part of the favor Allah told them to remember. {reward}He separated the sea, saved them, and drowned Pharaoh's people{/reward} {idea}while they were looking on.{/idea} They did not hear about it. They saw it.
now: The job came through on the last day. The scan came back clear. The money arrived the week rent was due. {trap}A month later, you call it luck.{/trap} {idea}You were looking on. Remember who parted the sea.{/idea}
old: That close call worked out because I was lucky.
new: The rescues I have seen with my own eyes were from Allah.
try: Write down one rescue in your life you witnessed. Keep it where you will see it.

title: Forty nights away, and they made a calf.
subtitle: How fast people slip once the guide is gone
then: Musa went to meet his Lord for forty nights, soon after they crossed the sea. {trap}In his absence, they took the calf for worship, and so wronged themselves.{/trap} The miracle at the sea was still fresh.
now: Ramadan ends and by Shawwal the night prayers are gone. Your teacher moves away and your study habit stops. {trap}When the person who held you steady leaves, it is shocking how fast things slip.{/trap}
old: After a strong spiritual moment, I will stay on track.
new: Even after great signs, I can slip fast once my support is gone.
try: Set one small habit today that does not depend on anyone else to keep it going.

title: Even after the calf, Allah forgave them.
subtitle: Forgiveness meant to produce gratitude
then: Ibn Kathir says Allah reminds them: {reward}remember My favor when I forgave you for worshipping the calf.{/reward} {idea}The purpose of the forgiveness is named in the verse itself: that you might be grateful.{/idea}
now: Someone forgave you for something big: a spouse, a parent, a friend you let down. {reward}You felt the relief.{/reward} {idea}The way to honor that forgiveness is to live differently because of it.{/idea} Allah's forgiveness asks the same.
old: Once I am forgiven, the matter is closed.
new: Being forgiven is a gift meant to make me grateful and change me.
try: Think of one sin you believe Allah forgave you. Thank Him for it in your own words.
